records.source: שָׁמוֹר֙ אֶת־חֹ֣דֶשׁ הָאָבִ֔יב וְעָשִׂ֣יתָ פֶּ֔סַח לַיהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֶ֑יךָ כִּ֞י בְּחֹ֣דֶשׁ הָֽאָבִ֗יב הוֹצִ֨יאֲךָ֜ יְהוָ֧ה אֱלֹהֶ֛יךָ מִמִּצְרַ֖יִם לָֽיְלָה׃
records.gloss: Keep the month of the Abib, and you shall do [the] Passover to Yahweh your God, for in [the] month of the Abib brought you out Yahweh your God from Egypt [by] night.
pieces: Observe the month of Abib by keeping the Passover for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, because it was in the month of Abib, at night, that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God brought you out of Egypt.

L.1: Keep the month of Abib, and you shall observe [the] Passover to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, for in the month of Abib {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God brought you out from Egypt by night.

R.1: Keep the Passover for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God in the month of Abib, in the spring. It was in that month, at night, that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God brought you out of Egypt.

decisions.choice: the month of Abib: the spring month of the exodus
decisions.reason: Abib means "fresh ears of grain". It is the month when the barley ripens, in March or April, and the month in which Israel left Egypt (Exodus 13:4; 23:15; 34:18). It is the first month of the festival year (Exodus 12:2), later called Nisan (Esther 3:7).

decisions.choice: keep the month ... do the Passover: hold the Passover at its proper time
decisions.reason: To "keep" the month is to watch over its date and what belongs to it. The verb "do" with "Passover" means to hold the Passover, both its sacrifice (verse 2) and its meal (verse 7), as in Exodus 12:47-48 and Numbers 9:2-5. Verses 1-8 bring together the Passover and the seven days of unleavened bread.

decisions.choice: by night: the night the LORD struck Egypt
decisions.reason: The LORD struck the firstborn of Egypt at midnight, and Pharaoh sent Israel away that same night (Exodus 12:29-31, 42). Numbers 33:3 says the people set out on the fifteenth day, the day after the Passover; the night is when the release began.

decisions.choice: in the spring
decisions.reason: Readable adds "in the spring" so that a reader who does not know the Hebrew month names can place Abib in the year (see the meaning decision).

records.heading: The Passover

records.source: וְזָבַ֥חְתָּ פֶּ֛סַח לַיהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ צֹ֣אן וּבָקָ֑ר בַּמָּקוֹם֙ אֲשֶׁר־יִבְחַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה לְשַׁכֵּ֥ן שְׁמ֖וֹ שָֽׁם׃
records.gloss: And you shall sacrifice [the] Passover to Yahweh your God, flock and herd, in the place that will choose Yahweh to make dwell his name there.
pieces: Sacrifice the Passover to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, from your flock or your herd, at the place {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will choose as a dwelling for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name.

L.2: And you shall sacrifice the Passover to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, [from the] flock and [the] herd, in the place which {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will choose to make {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name dwell there.

R.2: Sacrifice the Passover animal for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. It may come from your sheep and goats or from your cattle. Do it at the place {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will choose as the home for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name.

decisions.choice: flock and herd: animals from the sheep and goats or from the cattle
alternatives: the Passover animal itself may be from the flock or the herd
the flock is for the Passover, the herd for the festival's other sacrifices
decisions.reason: Exodus 12:3-5 says the Passover animal is a lamb or a kid from the flock. Here cattle are named too. This may mean that the Passover could also be a bull or cow, or it may take in the other sacrifices eaten during the festival week, as when the kings gave both flock animals and cattle for the Passover (2 Chronicles 30:24; 35:7-9). The text does not settle which.

decisions.choice: the place the LORD will choose: one sanctuary for the whole people
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy 12:5-14 commands that sacrifices be brought only to the one place the LORD chooses, not to any place of worship. Here that rule is applied to the Passover: in Egypt it was killed and eaten in each home (Exodus 12:3-7, 22), but in the land it is to be sacrificed at the sanctuary (verses 5-6).

decisions.choice: to make his name dwell there: to make the place his own, where he is known and present
decisions.reason: The name stands for the LORD himself as he makes himself known. Where he sets his name, that place belongs to him and is where his people meet him (12:5, 11; 1 Kings 8:29; Jeremiah 7:12).

decisions.choice: as a dwelling for his name / to be the home of his name
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn "to make his name dwell there" into a noun phrase, which reads more easily in a sentence that repeats it; the sense is the same. Literal keeps the verb. Readable also says "sheep and goats" for the flock and "cattle" for the herd, and supplies "animal" after "Passover".

records.source: לֹא־תֹאכַ֤ל עָלָיו֙ חָמֵ֔ץ שִׁבְעַ֥ת יָמִ֛ים תֹּֽאכַל־עָלָ֥יו מַצּ֖וֹת לֶ֣חֶם עֹ֑נִי כִּ֣י בְחִפָּז֗וֹן יָצָ֨אתָ֙ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם לְמַ֣עַן תִּזְכֹּר֔אֶת־י֤וֹם צֵֽאתְךָ֙ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם כֹּ֖ל יְמֵ֥י חַיֶּֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: Not you shall eat with it leaven; seven days you shall eat with it unleavened bread, bread of affliction, for in haste you came out from [the] land of Egypt, so that you may remember [the] day of your coming out from [the] land of Egypt all [the] days of your life.
pieces: Do not eat bread made with yeast with it. For seven days eat bread made without yeast with it, the bread of affliction, because you left the land of Egypt in a hurry. Do this so that all your life you will remember the day you came out of the land of Egypt.

L.3: You shall not eat leavened [bread] with it; seven days you shall eat unleavened bread with it, the bread of affliction, for in haste you came out from the land of Egypt, so that you may remember the day of your coming out from the land of Egypt all the days of your life.

R.3: Do not eat bread made with yeast with the Passover. For seven days eat bread made without yeast. It is the bread of hard times, because you left Egypt in a hurry. Eating it will help you remember all your life the day you came out of Egypt.

decisions.choice: with it: with the Passover sacrifice and the festival it begins
decisions.reason: "It" is the Passover of verse 2. The bread is eaten with the sacrifice on the first evening, and the same word "with it" carries on through the seven days, so the whole week of unleavened bread is joined to the Passover (Exodus 12:8, 15-20).

decisions.choice: bread of affliction: bread that recalls hardship
decisions.reason: The word for affliction is used of Israel's suffering in Egypt (Exodus 3:7; Deuteronomy 26:7). Flat bread baked in haste recalls both the hard life there and the hurried departure (Exodus 12:39).

decisions.choice: in haste you came out: the departure of Exodus 12
decisions.reason: Israel was sent out so quickly that the dough had no time to rise, and they baked it flat on the way (Exodus 12:11, 33-34, 39).

decisions.choice: bread made with yeast / bread made without yeast
decisions.reason: As in Leviticus 23:6, Balanced and Readable say "made without yeast" for unleavened bread; Literal keeps "leavened" and "unleavened bread". Readable says "bread of hard times" for "bread of affliction", and "with the Passover" for "with it".

records.source: וְלֹֽא־יֵרָאֶ֨ה לְךָ֥ שְׂאֹ֛ר בְּכָל־גְּבֻלְךָ֖ שִׁבְעַ֣ת יָמִ֑ים וְלֹא־יָלִ֣ין מִן־הַבָּשָׂ֗ר אֲשֶׁ֨ר תִּזְבַּ֥ח בָּעֶ֛רֶב בַּיּ֥וֹם הָרִאשׁ֖וֹן לַבֹּֽקֶר׃
records.gloss: And not shall be seen with you leaven in all your territory seven days, and not shall remain overnight from the meat that you sacrifice in the evening on the day the first until the morning.
pieces: For seven days no yeast is to be seen anywhere in your land. And none of the meat you sacrifice on the evening of the first day may be left over until morning.

L.4: And no leaven shall be seen with you in all your territory seven days, and none of the meat which you sacrifice in the evening on the first day shall remain overnight until the morning.

R.4: For seven days there must be no yeast anywhere in your land. And do not leave any of the meat you sacrifice on the evening of the first day until the next morning.

decisions.choice: leaven: a piece of fermented dough used to make bread rise
decisions.reason: This is a different word from the leavened bread of verse 3. It names the sour dough kept back from one baking to raise the next. None may be found in any house in the land for the seven days (Exodus 12:15, 19; 13:7).

decisions.choice: the meat you sacrifice in the evening on the first day: the Passover meat
decisions.reason: The first day is the Passover evening that begins the festival (verse 6; Exodus 12:6, 18). The rule that none of its meat be left until morning is the rule of Exodus 12:10 and 34:25.

decisions.choice: yeast; anywhere in your land
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "yeast" for leaven, as with the bread in verse 3, and "anywhere in your land" for "in all your territory". Literal keeps "leaven" and "territory".

records.source: לֹ֥א תוּכַ֖ל לִזְבֹּ֣חַ אֶת־הַפָּ֑סַח בְּאַחַ֣ד שְׁעָרֶ֔יךָ אֲשֶׁר־יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ נֹתֵ֥ן לָֽךְ׃
records.gloss: Not you are able to sacrifice the Passover in one of your gates which Yahweh your God [is] giving to you,
pieces: You may not sacrifice the Passover in just any of the towns {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is giving you,

L.5: You may not sacrifice the Passover in any one of your gates which {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is giving you,

R.5: Do not sacrifice the Passover animal in just any town that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is giving you.

decisions.choice: you are not able: you are not allowed
decisions.reason: "Not be able" here means that something is forbidden, not that it cannot be done, as in 12:17 and 17:15.

decisions.choice: your gates: your towns
decisions.reason: The gate of a walled town stood for the town itself, since its business and its courts were held there (verse 18; 21:19; Ruth 4:1). "In one of your gates" means in any town of your own choosing, away from the chosen place (12:17-18).

decisions.choice: towns
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "towns" for "gates" here and through the chapter (verses 11, 14, 18). Literal keeps "gates". Balanced ends with a comma, as Literal does, because the sentence runs on into verse 6.

records.source: כִּ֠י אִֽם־אֶל־הַמָּק֞וֹם אֲשֶׁר־יִבְחַ֨ר יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֶ֨יךָ֙ לְשַׁכֵּ֣ן שְׁמ֔וֹ שָׁ֛ם תִּזְבַּ֥ח אֶת־הַפֶּ֖סַח בָּעָ֑רֶב כְּב֣וֹא הַשֶּׁ֔מֶשׁ מוֹעֵ֖ד צֵֽאתְךָ֥ מִמִּצְרָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: but only at the place which will choose Yahweh your God to make dwell his name there, there you shall sacrifice the Passover in the evening, at [the] going in of the sun, [the] appointed time of your coming out from Egypt.
pieces: but only at the place {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God will choose as a dwelling for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name. There you are to sacrifice the Passover in the evening, as the sun goes down, at the time of day you came out of Egypt.

L.6: but only at the place which {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God will choose to make {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name dwell there; there you shall sacrifice the Passover in the evening, at the going in of the sun, at the appointed time of your coming out from Egypt.

R.6: Sacrifice it only at the place {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God will choose as the home for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name. Do it in the evening, at sunset. That is the time of day when you left Egypt.

decisions.choice: but only: the one place set against any town
decisions.reason: The two words together mean "except" or "but only", and they set the chosen place against the "any one of your gates" of verse 5. The repeated "there" fixes the sacrifice to that place.

decisions.choice: the appointed time of your coming out: the hour of the day when Israel went out
alternatives: the season or anniversary of the exodus
decisions.reason: The word means a set time. It could name the season or the date of the exodus, but joined to "in the evening, at sunset" it points to the hour. Exodus 12:6 has the lamb killed "between the two evenings", and the night of the exodus followed (Exodus 12:42).

decisions.choice: the going in of the sun: sunset
decisions.reason: The sun "goes in" when it sets. The Passover was killed in the evening and eaten that night (Exodus 12:6, 8).

decisions.choice: at the time of day
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "the time of day" to make clear that the appointed time is the hour (see the meaning decision). Readable starts a new sentence, since its verse 5 ended with a full stop, and supplies "Sacrifice it".

records.source: וּבִשַּׁלְתָּ֙ וְאָ֣כַלְתָּ֔ בַּמָּק֕וֹם אֲשֶׁ֥ר יִבְחַ֛ר יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ בּ֑וֹ וּפָנִ֣יתָ בַבֹּ֔קֶר וְהָלַכְתָּ֖ לְאֹהָלֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: And you shall cook and you shall eat in the place which will choose Yahweh your God in it, and you shall turn in the morning and go to your tents.
pieces: Cook it and eat it at the place {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God will choose. Then in the morning turn back and go to your tents.

L.7: And you shall cook [it] and eat [it] at the place which {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God will choose, and in the morning you shall turn and go to your tents.

R.7: Cook the meat and eat it at the place {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God will choose. The next morning, start back and go to your tents.

decisions.choice: cook: prepare the meat, not necessarily by boiling
decisions.reason: The verb often means to boil (Exodus 29:31; 1 Samuel 2:13-15), and Exodus 12:9 forbids eating the Passover boiled in water and commands it roasted. But the verb can mean to cook in general: 2 Chronicles 35:13 uses it of the Passover "in the fire", that is, roasted. Here it is taken in that general sense, which agrees with Exodus 12. Some take it as boiling, which would differ from Exodus 12:9.

decisions.choice: go to your tents: go back to where you are staying, or go home
alternatives: return to your lodgings at the place
decisions.reason: "To your tents" can mean "home" even after Israel lived in houses (1 Kings 8:66; 12:16). Here it may mean leaving the sanctuary for home the morning after the Passover, or going back to the lodgings near the sanctuary for the rest of the week. Verse 8 gives a gathering on the seventh day but does not say where.

decisions.choice: it / the meat
decisions.reason: Hebrew leaves the object of "cook" and "eat" unstated. Literal brackets "[it]"; Balanced says "it", and Readable "the meat". All three keep "your tents", since the text leaves open where the people go (see the meaning decision).

records.source: שֵׁ֥שֶׁת יָמִ֖ים תֹּאכַ֣ל מַצּ֑וֹת וּבַיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִ֗י עֲצֶ֨רֶת֙ לַיהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ לֹ֥א תַעֲשֶׂ֖ה מְלָאכָֽה׃ס
records.gloss: Six days you shall eat unleavened bread, and on the day the seventh [is] a solemn assembly to Yahweh your God; not you shall do work.
pieces: For six days eat bread made without yeast, and on the seventh day hold a solemn assembly for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. Do no work on it.

L.8: Six days you shall eat unleavened bread, and on the seventh day [there shall be] a solemn assembly to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God; you shall not do work.

R.8: For six days eat bread made without yeast. On the seventh day, hold a special gathering that ends the festival, to worship {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. Do not do any work that day.

decisions.choice: six days ... and on the seventh day: the seven days of verse 3
decisions.reason: Verse 3 gives seven days of unleavened bread. Here the week is told as six days followed by a seventh with its gathering, as in Exodus 13:6, so the total is the same seven days.

decisions.choice: a solemn assembly: a gathering on a day when work is held back
decisions.reason: As at Leviticus 23:36, the word comes from a verb meaning to hold back. It names the gathering on the last day of the festival, when the people stop work and meet for worship (Leviticus 23:8; Numbers 28:25).

decisions.choice: work: the ordinary work of a working day
decisions.reason: Leviticus 23:8 and Numbers 28:25 say "no work of labor" for this day. Here the shorter "no work" stands for the same rule.

decisions.choice: a special gathering that ends the festival
decisions.reason: As at Leviticus 23:36 and Numbers 29:35, Readable says what the solemn assembly is. Literal and Balanced keep "a solemn assembly".

records.source: שִׁבְעָ֥ה שָׁבֻעֹ֖ת תִּסְפָּר־לָ֑ךְ מֵהָחֵ֤ל חֶרְמֵשׁ֙ בַּקָּמָ֔ה תָּחֵ֣ל לִסְפֹּ֔ר שִׁבְעָ֖ה שָׁבֻעֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: Seven weeks you shall count for yourself; from [the] beginning of [the] sickle on the standing grain you shall begin to count seven weeks.
pieces: Count seven weeks. Begin counting the seven weeks from the time you first put the sickle to the standing grain.

L.9: Seven weeks you shall count for yourself; from the beginning of the sickle on the standing grain you shall begin to count seven weeks.

R.9: Count seven weeks, starting from the day you first begin to cut your grain.

decisions.choice: the beginning of the sickle on the standing grain: the start of the grain harvest
decisions.reason: The first cutting of grain is the barley harvest in the spring. Leviticus 23:15-16 counts the seven weeks from the day the first sheaf is waved before the LORD; here the count is tied to the start of reaping, which is the same season.

decisions.choice: standing grain: grain still growing in the field
decisions.reason: The word names grain not yet cut (23:26; Exodus 22:5).

decisions.choice: the day you first begin to cut your grain
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what putting the sickle to the standing grain means, and joins the two halves of the verse, which say the same thing twice, into one sentence.

records.heading: The Festival of Weeks

records.source: וְעָשִׂ֜יתָ חַ֤ג שָׁבֻעוֹת֙ לַיהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ מִסַּ֛ת נִדְבַ֥ת יָדְךָ֖ אֲשֶׁ֣ר תִּתֵּ֑ן כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר יְבָרֶכְךָ֖ יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: And you shall do [the] festival of weeks to Yahweh your God, [the] sufficiency of [the] freewill offering of your hand which you shall give, just as blesses you Yahweh your God.
pieces: Then keep the Festival of Weeks for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, bringing a freewill offering from your own hand, as much as fits the way {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God has blessed you.

L.10: And you shall keep the festival of weeks to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God [with] the measure of the freewill offering of your hand, which you shall give just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God blesses you.

R.10: Then celebrate the Festival of Weeks to honor {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. Bring a gift that you choose to give. Make it as large as the blessing {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God has given you.

decisions.choice: the festival of weeks: the festival at the end of the grain harvest
decisions.reason: It takes its name from the seven weeks of verse 9 and falls on the fiftieth day (Leviticus 23:15-21). Exodus 23:16 calls it the Festival of Harvest, and Numbers 28:26 the day of firstfruits.

decisions.choice: the sufficiency: the amount that matches
decisions.reason: The word is found only here. It seems to mean "what is enough for" or "in proportion to": the gift is measured by how much the LORD has given.

decisions.choice: freewill offering of your hand: a gift given by choice
decisions.reason: A freewill offering is one that is not required by a vow or a law, but given willingly (Leviticus 7:16; 22:18-23; Exodus 35:29). "Of your hand" means given by you, from what you have.

decisions.choice: Festival of Weeks; has blessed
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable write the festival's name with capitals, as in Leviticus 23 and Numbers 28:26; Literal keeps "festival of weeks". The Hebrew verb "blesses" can look back or forward; Balanced and Readable say "has blessed", because the gift at harvest is measured by the crop already gathered. Readable says "to honor" for "to the LORD".

records.source: וְשָׂמַחְתָּ֞ לִפְנֵ֣י׀יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֗יךָ אַתָּ֨ה וּבִנְךָ֣ וּבִתֶּךָ֮ וְעַבְדְּךָ֣ וַאֲמָתֶךָ֒ וְהַלֵּוִי֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בִּשְׁעָרֶ֔יךָ וְהַגֵּ֛ר וְהַיָּת֥וֹם וְהָאַלְמָנָ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּקִרְבֶּ֑ךָ בַּמָּק֗וֹם אֲשֶׁ֤ר יִבְחַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ לְשַׁכֵּ֥ן שְׁמ֖וֹ שָֽׁם׃
records.gloss: And you shall rejoice before Yahweh your God, you and your son and your daughter and your male slave and your female slave and the Levite who [is] in your gates and the sojourner and the fatherless and the widow who [are] in your midst, in the place which will choose Yahweh your God to make dwell his name there.
pieces: Rejoice before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, you and your son and daughter, your male and female servants, the Levite who lives in your towns, and the outsider, the fatherless child and the widow who live among you. Rejoice at the place {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God will choose as a dwelling for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name.

L.11: And you shall rejoice before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, you and your son and your daughter and your male slave and your female slave, and the Levite who [is] within your gates, and the sojourner and the fatherless and the widow who [are] in your midst, in the place which {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God will choose to make {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name dwell there.

R.11: Celebrate with joy before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God at the place {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God will choose as the home for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name. Celebrate together with your sons and daughters, your servants, the Levites who live in your towns, and the strangers, the children whose fathers have died, and the widows who live among you.

decisions.choice: rejoice before the LORD: a festival meal of joy in his presence
decisions.reason: "Before the LORD" means at his sanctuary. Deuteronomy often joins rejoicing to the meals eaten there (12:7, 12, 18; 14:26). The joy is shared with the whole household.

decisions.choice: the Levite, the sojourner, the fatherless, the widow: people with no land or family to provide for them
decisions.reason: The Levites had no share of the land (12:12; 14:27, 29). The sojourner was an outsider living in Israel without family land, the fatherless child had lost a father, and the widow a husband. Deuteronomy names them together as those who must be included in the harvest and the feasts (14:29; 24:19-21; 26:12).

decisions.choice: male slave, female slave: servants owned by the household
decisions.reason: The words name people who belonged to the household and worked for it (15:12-18). They too share the festival.

decisions.choice: servants; outsider / strangers; fatherless child / children whose fathers have died
decisions.reason: Literal says "male slave" and "female slave"; Balanced and Readable say "servants", following the style guide's rule for this word. Literal keeps "sojourner", Balanced says "outsider" and Readable "strangers", as in Leviticus 19:10, 34. Readable explains "fatherless", as in Exodus 22:21, and uses plurals for the Hebrew singulars, which stand for every such person.

decisions.choice: Rejoice at the place ... / Celebrate together with ...
decisions.reason: The Hebrew puts the place at the end, after a long list. Balanced repeats "Rejoice" so the place can stand in a sentence of its own; Readable names the place first and repeats "Celebrate" before the list.

records.source: וְזָ֣כַרְתָּ֔ כִּי־עֶ֥בֶד הָיִ֖יתָ בְּמִצְרָ֑יִם וְשָׁמַרְתָּ֣ וְעָשִׂ֔יתָ אֶת־הַֽחֻקִּ֖ים הָאֵֽלֶּה׃פ
records.gloss: And you shall remember that a slave you were in Egypt, and you shall keep and do the statutes the these.
pieces: Remember that you were slaves in Egypt, and be careful to keep these statutes.

L.12: And you shall remember that you were a slave in Egypt, and you shall be careful to do these statutes.

R.12: Remember that you were slaves in Egypt. Be careful to obey these laws.

decisions.choice: remember that you were a slave: the reason for sharing the feast
decisions.reason: Israel's own past in Egypt is the ground for including servants, outsiders, orphans and widows in the rejoicing (verse 11), as in 5:15, 15:15 and 24:18, 22.

decisions.choice: keep and do: carefully carry out
decisions.reason: The two verbs together, common in Deuteronomy (5:1; 6:3), mean to obey with care.

decisions.choice: slave; slaves
decisions.reason: Every level keeps "slave", because Israel's slavery in Egypt is the point, as the style guide directs. The Hebrew singular addresses Israel as one person; Balanced and Readable use the plural, which says the same in English. Readable says "laws" for "statutes".

records.source: חַ֧ג הַסֻּכֹּ֛ת תַּעֲשֶׂ֥ה לְךָ֖ שִׁבְעַ֣ת יָמִ֑ים בְּאָ֨סְפְּךָ֔ מִֽגָּרְנְךָ֖ וּמִיִּקְבֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: [The] festival of the booths you shall do for yourself seven days, when you gather from your threshing floor and from your winepress.
pieces: Keep the Festival of Booths for seven days, when you have gathered in the harvest from your threshing floor and your winepress.

L.13: The festival of booths you shall keep for yourself seven days, when you gather in from your threshing floor and from your winepress.

R.13: Celebrate the Festival of Booths for seven days. Hold it after you have gathered your grain from the threshing floor and your grapes from the winepress.

decisions.choice: the festival of booths: the festival of living in huts made of branches
decisions.reason: For seven days Israel lived in booths, rough shelters of branches, in memory of the journey from Egypt (Leviticus 23:34, 42-43). Exodus 23:16 calls it the Festival of Ingathering.

decisions.choice: when you gather from your threshing floor and your winepress: at the end of the year's harvest
decisions.reason: The threshing floor is where grain was beaten out and winnowed; the winepress is where grapes, and also olives, were pressed (15:14; Numbers 18:27). The festival comes in the autumn, when all the year's crops are in (Leviticus 23:39).

decisions.choice: the harvest / your grain ... your grapes
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "when you gather from" the threshing floor and the winepress. Balanced supplies "the harvest" and Readable names the grain and the grapes, which those places imply. Readable splits the verse into two sentences.

records.heading: The Festival of Booths

records.source: וְשָׂמַחְתָּ֖ בְּחַגֶּ֑ךָ אַתָּ֨ה וּבִנְךָ֤ וּבִתֶּ֨ךָ֙ וְעַבְדְּךָ֣ וַאֲמָתֶ֔ךָ וְהַלֵּוִ֗י וְהַגֵּ֛ר וְהַיָּת֥וֹם וְהָאַלְמָנָ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר בִּשְׁעָרֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: And you shall rejoice in your festival, you and your son and your daughter and your male slave and your female slave and the Levite and the sojourner and the fatherless and the widow who [are] in your gates.
pieces: Rejoice at your festival, you and your son and daughter, your male and female servants, and the Levite, the outsider, the fatherless child and the widow who live in your towns.

L.14: And you shall rejoice in your festival, you and your son and your daughter and your male slave and your female slave, and the Levite and the sojourner and the fatherless and the widow who [are] within your gates.

R.14: Be full of joy at your festival, together with your sons and daughters, your servants, and the Levites, strangers, children whose fathers have died, and widows who live in your towns.

decisions.choice: rejoice in your festival: the same shared joy as at Weeks
decisions.reason: The list repeats that of verse 11 (see the notes there). Here "who are in your gates" covers the Levite and the three others together. Leviticus 23:40 also commands rejoicing at this festival.

decisions.choice: servants; outsider / strangers; fatherless child / children whose fathers have died
decisions.reason: As in verse 11.

records.source: שִׁבְעַ֣ת יָמִ֗ים תָּחֹג֙ לַיהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ בַּמָּק֖וֹם אֲשֶׁר־יִבְחַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה כִּ֣י יְבָרֶכְךָ֞ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֗יךָ בְּכֹ֤ל תְּבוּאָֽתְךָ֙ וּבְכֹל֙ מַעֲשֵׂ֣ה יָדֶ֔יךָ וְהָיִ֖יתָ אַ֥ךְ שָׂמֵֽחַ׃
records.gloss: Seven days you shall keep festival to Yahweh your God in the place which will choose Yahweh, for will bless you Yahweh your God in all your produce and in all [the] work of your hands, and you shall be surely joyful.
pieces: For seven days keep the festival for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God at the place {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will choose. For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God will bless you in all your harvest and in all that your hands do, and you are to be nothing but joyful.

L.15: Seven days you shall keep the festival to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God at the place which {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will choose, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God will bless you in all your produce and in all the work of your hands, and you shall be altogether joyful.

R.15: Celebrate this festival for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God for seven days at the place {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will choose. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God will bless all your crops and all the work you do. So be full of joy.

decisions.choice: for the LORD will bless you: the reason for the festival
decisions.reason: The festival is kept because the LORD gives the harvest and the fruit of all work. The verb can look forward ("will bless") or describe what he does ("blesses"); either way the blessing is the ground of the joy.

decisions.choice: you shall be surely joyful: be wholly glad
alternatives: and you will be altogether joyful (a promise)
decisions.reason: The small word before "joyful" means "only" or "surely": nothing is to spoil the gladness. The verb form can be a command ("you are to be") or a promise ("you will be"); in a list of instructions it is taken as a command.

decisions.choice: produce: the yield of the land
decisions.reason: The word means what the land brings in, grain, wine and oil (14:22, 28).

decisions.choice: nothing but joyful / So be full of joy
decisions.reason: Balanced says "nothing but joyful" for the strong "surely joyful" and Readable "full of joy". Literal says "altogether joyful". Readable says "crops" for "produce".

records.source: שָׁל֣וֹשׁ פְּעָמִ֣ים׀בַּשָּׁנָ֡ה יֵרָאֶ֨ה כָל־זְכוּרְךָ֜ אֶת־פְּנֵ֣י׀יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֗יךָ בַּמָּקוֹם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יִבְחָ֔ר בְּחַ֧ג הַמַּצּ֛וֹת וּבְחַ֥ג הַשָּׁבֻע֖וֹת וּבְחַ֣ג הַסֻּכּ֑וֹת וְלֹ֧א יֵרָאֶ֛ה אֶת־פְּנֵ֥י יְהוָ֖ה רֵיקָֽם׃
records.gloss: Three times in the year shall appear all your males [before the] face of Yahweh your God in the place which he will choose: at [the] festival of the unleavened bread and at [the] festival of the weeks and at [the] festival of the booths; and not shall appear [before the] face of Yahweh empty.
pieces: Every male among you is to appear before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God three times a year, at the place {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will choose. The three times are the Festival of Unleavened Bread, the Festival of Weeks and the Festival of Booths. None of them is to come before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} with empty hands.

L.16: Three times in the year all your males shall appear before the face of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God at the place which {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will choose: at the festival of unleavened bread, and at the festival of weeks, and at the festival of booths; and none shall appear before the face of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} empty.

R.16: Three times every year, all your men and boys must come and stand before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God at the place {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will choose. They must come for the Festival of Unleavened Bread, the Festival of Weeks, and the Festival of Booths. No one should come to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} without bringing a gift.

decisions.choice: all your males: the men were required to come
decisions.reason: As in Exodus 23:17 and 34:23, the duty to go to the sanctuary was laid on the males. Women and children often came as well, as verses 11 and 14 show.

decisions.choice: appear before the face of the LORD: come into his presence at the sanctuary
decisions.reason: The verb as the Hebrew text is pointed means "be seen" before the LORD's face. As at Exodus 23:15, the same consonants could be read "see the face of the LORD".

decisions.choice: empty: without an offering
decisions.reason: No one is to come with nothing to give (Exodus 23:15; 34:20). Verse 17 says how much each is to bring.

decisions.choice: Festival of Unleavened Bread, Festival of Weeks, Festival of Booths
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the festival names with capitals, as in Leviticus 23 and verses 10 and 13; Literal keeps them lowercase. Readable says "men and boys" for "males", as in Exodus 23:17, and "without bringing a gift" for "empty".

records.source: אִ֖ישׁ כְּמַתְּנַ֣ת יָד֑וֹ כְּבִרְכַּ֛ת יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ אֲשֶׁ֥ר נָֽתַן־לָֽךְ׃ס
records.gloss: Each according to [the] gift of his hand, according to [the] blessing of Yahweh your God which he has given to you.
pieces: Each of them is to give as he is able, in keeping with the blessing {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God has given you.

L.17: Each man [shall give] according to the gift of his hand, according to the blessing of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God which {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has given you.

R.17: Each one should give as much as he can, depending on how much {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God has blessed you.

decisions.choice: the gift of his hand: what he is able to give
decisions.reason: "His hand" stands for what a person has and can give (as "your hand" in verse 10). The gift is not a fixed amount.

decisions.choice: each according to the blessing: the gift matches what the LORD has given
decisions.reason: "Each" is each of the males of verse 16. The sentence has no verb; "give" is understood from verses 10 and 16. The gift is measured by the blessing received, as in verse 10.

decisions.choice: shall give / is to give / should give
decisions.reason: All three levels supply the verb the Hebrew leaves unstated; Literal brackets it.

records.source: שֹׁפְטִ֣ים וְשֹֽׁטְרִ֗ים תִּֽתֶּן־לְךָ֙ בְּכָל־שְׁעָרֶ֔יךָ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יְהוָ֧ה אֱלֹהֶ֛יךָ נֹתֵ֥ן לְךָ֖ לִשְׁבָטֶ֑יךָ וְשָׁפְט֥וּ אֶת־הָעָ֖ם מִשְׁפַּט־צֶֽדֶק׃
records.gloss: Judges and officials you shall give for yourself in all your gates which Yahweh your God [is] giving to you, by your tribes, and they shall judge the people [with] judgment of righteousness.
pieces: Appoint judges and officials for each of your tribes in all the towns {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is giving you, and they are to judge the people with fair judgment.

L.18: Judges and officials you shall appoint for yourself in all your gates which {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is giving you, according to your tribes, and they shall judge the people [with] judgment of righteousness.

R.18: Choose judges and officials for each of your tribes in every town {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God gives you. They must judge the people fairly.

decisions.choice: officials: officers who served the leaders and carried out their orders
decisions.reason: The word may come from a root meaning to write, and these men seem to have kept records and enforced decisions. They appear with the slave drivers in Egypt (Exodus 5:6, 14), with the leaders of the tribes (1:15; 29:9) and in the army (20:5).

decisions.choice: in all your gates, by your tribes: local courts in every town
decisions.reason: The town gate was where cases were heard (21:19; 22:15; Ruth 4:1-2). Each tribe's towns were to have their own judges. This verse begins a new section on those who lead the people: judges, kings, priests and prophets (16:18-18:22).

decisions.choice: judgment of righteousness: right and fair judgment
decisions.reason: The words mean judgment that is right by God's standard, giving each one what is due (1:16; Leviticus 19:15).

decisions.choice: appoint / choose; fair judgment / fairly
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "give" judges, meaning to appoint them. Balanced and Readable say "fair judgment" or "fairly" for "judgment of righteousness", as in Leviticus 19:15; Literal keeps the Hebrew phrase.

records.heading: Judges and justice

records.source: לֹא־תַטֶּ֣ה מִשְׁפָּ֔ט לֹ֥א תַכִּ֖יר פָּנִ֑ים וְלֹא־תִקַּ֣ח שֹׁ֔חַד כִּ֣י הַשֹּׁ֗חַד יְעַוֵּר֙ עֵינֵ֣י חֲכָמִ֔ים וִֽיסַלֵּ֖ף דִּבְרֵ֥י צַדִּיקִֽם׃
records.gloss: Not you shall turn aside justice; not you shall recognize faces; and not you shall take a bribe, for the bribe blinds [the] eyes of wise [people] and twists [the] words of righteous [people].
pieces: Do not bend justice, and do not favor anyone because of who they are. Take no bribe, for a bribe makes even the wise blind and overturns the pleas of those in the right.

L.19: You shall not turn aside justice; you shall not recognize faces; and you shall not take a bribe, for the bribe blinds the eyes of the wise and twists the words of the righteous.

R.19: Never be unfair in judging. Do not treat some people better than others. Never accept money or gifts to change your decision. Bribes keep even wise people from seeing clearly, and they twist the case of people who are in the right.

decisions.choice: turn aside justice: make a judgment lean away from what is right
decisions.reason: The verb means to bend or turn aside. To bend justice is to give a wrong verdict (24:17; 27:19; Exodus 23:6).

decisions.choice: recognize faces: show favor to someone because of who they are
decisions.reason: To "recognize the face" of a person in court is to take sides because of their rank, wealth or friendship, rather than the facts of the case (1:17; Leviticus 19:15).

decisions.choice: the words of the righteous: the case of those in the right
decisions.reason: As at Exodus 23:8, which this half of the verse repeats with "the wise" in place of "the clear-sighted": the words may be the pleas of the innocent party, which a bribe overturns, or the rulings of honest judges, which a bribe twists. The first fits the courtroom setting.

decisions.choice: favor anyone because of who they are; money or gifts to change your decision
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the idiom "recognize faces". Readable explains what a bribe is, as in Exodus 23:8, and keeps that verse's wording for the second half.

records.source: צֶ֥דֶק צֶ֖דֶק תִּרְדֹּ֑ף לְמַ֤עַן תִּֽחְיֶה֙ וְיָרַשְׁתָּ֣ אֶת־הָאָ֔רֶץ אֲשֶׁר־יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ נֹתֵ֥ן לָֽךְ׃ס
records.gloss: Righteousness, righteousness you shall pursue, so that you may live and take possession of the land which Yahweh your God [is] giving to you.
pieces: Pursue what is right, nothing but what is right, so that you may live and take possession of the land {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is giving you.

L.20: Righteousness, righteousness you shall pursue, so that you may live and take possession of the land that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is giving you.

R.20: Always do what is right and fair. Then you will live and take possession of the land {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is giving you.

decisions.choice: righteousness, righteousness: the word repeated for emphasis
decisions.reason: Saying the word twice makes it strong: right and nothing else, right in every case.

decisions.choice: righteousness ... pursue: chase after what is right
decisions.reason: The word means what is right and just, measured by God's standard (verse 18). In this setting of courts and judges it means justice done fairly. "Pursue" is the verb for running after something to catch it.

decisions.choice: so that you may live and take possession of the land: life in the land is tied to doing right
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy often joins obedience with life and the gift of the land (4:1; 5:33; 8:1).

decisions.choice: what is right, nothing but what is right / what is right and fair
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "what is right" for "righteousness", since here it is the conduct asked of judges and people. Balanced keeps the repetition with "nothing but"; Readable gives its force with "always". Literal keeps "righteousness, righteousness".

records.source: לֹֽא־תִטַּ֥ע לְךָ֛ אֲשֵׁרָ֖ה כָּל־עֵ֑ץ אֵ֗צֶל מִזְבַּ֛ח יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ אֲשֶׁ֥ר תַּעֲשֶׂה־לָּֽךְ׃ס
records.gloss: Not you shall plant for yourself [an] Asherah, any tree, beside [the] altar of Yahweh your God which you shall make for yourself.
pieces: Do not plant any tree as an Asherah pole beside the altar you build for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.

L.21: You shall not plant for yourself an Asherah pole, any tree, beside the altar of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God which you make for yourself.

R.21: Do not plant any kind of tree or wooden pole used to worship the goddess Asherah beside the altar you build for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.

decisions.choice: Asherah: an object of wood for the goddess Asherah
decisions.reason: As at Exodus 34:13, Asherah was a Canaanite goddess, and the word also names the wooden pole or tree that stood for her beside an altar (7:5; 12:3; Judges 6:25-26).

decisions.choice: plant an Asherah, any tree: a living tree, or a pole of any wood
alternatives: any wooden pole as an Asherah
decisions.reason: "Any tree" can mean any kind of living tree planted as an Asherah, or any kind of wood set in the ground as a pole. The verb "plant" fits a tree but can be used of setting something firmly in place (Ecclesiastes 12:11). Either way, no such object may stand by the LORD's altar.

decisions.choice: beside the altar of the LORD: no mixing of his worship with that of other gods
decisions.reason: The command forbids bringing Canaanite symbols into the worship of the LORD, even beside his own altar (12:2-4, 30-31). Verses 21-22 and 17:1 give rules for right worship.

decisions.choice: Asherah pole / tree or wooden pole used to worship the goddess Asherah
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced say "Asherah pole" and Readable explains the name, as the terms for this book direct. Readable says "tree or wooden pole" to keep both readings of "any tree" open (see the meaning decision).

records.source: וְלֹֽא־תָקִ֥ים לְךָ֖ מַצֵּבָ֑ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר שָׂנֵ֖א יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶֽיךָ׃ס
records.gloss: And not you shall raise up for yourself [a] pillar, which hates Yahweh your God.
pieces: And do not set up a standing stone, a thing {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God hates.

L.22: And you shall not set up for yourself a pillar, which {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God hates.

R.22: Do not set up a stone pillar used in worship. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God hates such pillars.

decisions.choice: pillar: a standing stone set up at a place of worship
decisions.reason: As at Exodus 23:24 and 34:13, these were upright stones that marked a god's presence at a shrine. The Canaanite pillars were to be broken down (7:5; 12:3).

decisions.choice: which the LORD your God hates: a practice once used, now forbidden
decisions.reason: Jacob and Moses had set up such stones to the LORD (Genesis 28:18; Exodus 24:4). Because the pillar belonged to the worship of other gods in the land, Israel is now forbidden to set one up even for the LORD. Things the LORD "hates" are things he rejects in worship (12:31).

decisions.choice: standing stone / stone pillar used in worship
decisions.reason: As at Exodus 34:13, Balanced and Readable say what the pillar was. Literal keeps "pillar". Readable makes the relative clause a sentence of its own.
